title: Nobel Prize Awarded to Economists for Stabilizing Global Markets
subtitle: Robert Hall and Michael Woodford are honored for developing tools that help governments manage economic ups and downs.

summary.en: Two American economists, Robert Hall and Michael Woodford, have won the 2026 Nobel Prize in economics. Their research created the 'New Keynesian' model, which helps central banks manage inflation and unemployment. By focusing on how families and businesses make decisions, their work provides a foundation for modern economic policy. The prize committee noted that these tools were essential during the 2008 financial crisis and the recent pandemic. While their methods are widely used, some experts continue to debate the best ways to communicate these policies to the public.
summary.zh: 兩位美國經濟學家霍爾與伍德福德榮獲二〇二六年諾貝爾經濟學獎。他們的研究建立了「新凱因斯」模型，協助中央銀行管理通貨膨脹與失業率。透過聚焦於家庭與企業如何做出決策，他們的研究為現代經濟政策奠定了基礎。獎項委員會指出，這些工具在二〇〇八年金融危機與近期疫情期間至關重要。儘管他們的方法被廣泛使用，部分專家仍持續辯論向大眾溝通這些政策的最佳方式。

paragraphs.en: Two American economists have been awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for their work on helping governments and central banks manage the economy. Robert Hall of Stanford University and Michael Woodford of Columbia University were honored for creating new ways to understand and control the 'boom-and-bust' cycles—the periods of rapid economic growth followed by sharp declines—that often cause high unemployment and rising prices.
paragraphs.zh: 兩位美國經濟學家因協助政府與中央銀行管理經濟的貢獻，榮獲二〇二六年諾貝爾經濟學獎。史丹佛大學的霍爾（Robert Hall）與哥倫比亞大學的伍德福德（Michael Woodford）因開創了理解並控制「繁榮與蕭條」週期的新方法而獲獎；這些週期指的是經濟快速成長後緊接著劇烈衰退的現象，往往會導致高失業率與物價上漲。

paragraphs.en: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences stated that the pair’s research led to a 'paradigm shift' in how countries handle economic stability. According to The Guardian Business, the award is worth a combined $1.2 million. The committee explained that the work of Hall and Woodford provides a stable foundation for the models used by central banks and finance ministries across the world today.
paragraphs.zh: 瑞典皇家科學院表示，兩人的研究促成了各國處理經濟穩定方式的「典範轉移」。根據《衛報商業版》報導，該獎項總獎金為一百二十萬美元。委員會解釋，霍爾與伍德福德的研究成果，為當今全球中央銀行與財政部所使用的模型提供了穩固的基礎。

paragraphs.en: To understand why this matters, one must look at the history of economic thought. After the Great Depression, the economist John Maynard Keynes argued that governments should step in to boost demand when the economy is weak or lower demand when prices rise too quickly. However, as NPR News reports, this traditional 'Keynesian recipe' struggled during the 1970s. At that time, many countries suffered from both high inflation and high unemployment at the same time, a situation the old models could not easily explain or fix.
paragraphs.zh: 要理解這項研究為何重要，必須回顧經濟思想史。在大蕭條之後，經濟學家凱因斯（John Maynard Keynes）主張，當經濟疲軟時，政府應介入以提振需求，或在物價上漲過快時抑制需求。然而，正如美國公共廣播電台報導，這種傳統的「凱因斯處方」在七〇年代面臨困境。當時許多國家同時飽受高通貨膨脹與高失業率之苦，這是舊有模型難以解釋或解決的狀況。

paragraphs.en: Hall and Woodford improved these ideas by focusing on the 'microeconomic foundations' of the economy. This means they looked at how individual households and businesses make decisions about spending and pricing. Instead of viewing the economy as a machine that leaders can simply control by pulling levers, their work shows that the economy is shaped by the choices of millions of people who are always looking toward the future.
paragraphs.zh: 霍爾與伍德福德透過聚焦於經濟的「個體經濟基礎」來改良這些觀點。這意味著他們研究了個別家庭與企業如何針對支出與定價做出決策。他們的理論顯示，經濟並非領導者可以透過拉動操縱桿來簡單控制的機器，而是由數百萬隨時展望未來的民眾所做的選擇而形塑而成。

paragraphs.en: According to NPR News, Hall focused on how families decide to spend money based on what they expect their future income to be. If people worry about 'dark clouds on the horizon,' they will start saving money today, which changes the economy. Meanwhile, Woodford focused on how businesses set prices. He noted that because it is often expensive for companies to change their prices, they try to plan ahead for a long period. Because both groups look to the future, the laureates argued that policymakers must communicate their plans clearly to the public.
paragraphs.zh: 根據美國公共廣播電台報導，霍爾專注於家庭如何根據對未來收入的預期來決定支出。如果民眾擔心「烏雲密布」，他們今天就會開始儲蓄，進而改變經濟走向。同時，伍德福德則專注於企業如何制定價格。他指出，由於企業調整價格通常成本高昂，因此他們會試圖為長期進行規劃。由於這兩類群體都展望未來，獲獎者主張決策者必須向大眾清楚溝通其計畫。

paragraphs.en: This idea led to a tool known as 'forward guidance.' This is a practice where central banks tell the public what they expect interest rates—the cost of borrowing money—to be in the future. This tool became very important after the 2008 financial crisis and during the Covid-19 pandemic, when interest rates were cut to record lows to help the economy survive. By explaining their goals, central banks can help people feel more confident, which keeps the economy moving.
paragraphs.zh: 這個概念引導出了一種稱為「前瞻指引」的工具。這是一種中央銀行向大眾說明未來利率（借貸資金的成本）預期走向的做法。此工具在二〇〇八年金融危機期間以及新冠肺炎疫情期間變得極為重要，當時利率被降至歷史低點以協助經濟存續。透過說明目標，中央銀行能協助民眾建立信心，進而維持經濟運作。

paragraphs.en: However, this approach is not without its critics. Some officials argue that forward guidance should only be used in a limited way to avoid confusion. The Guardian Business noted that in 2014, former Bank of England governor Mark Carney was even called an 'unreliable boyfriend' by some critics because he gave hints about interest rate changes that did not happen. Despite these challenges, the work of Hall and Woodford remains the main framework for modern economic policy.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，這種方法並非沒有批評者。部分官員主張，前瞻指引應僅在有限範圍內使用，以避免造成混亂。《衛報商業版》指出，二〇一四年時，前英格蘭銀行總裁卡尼（Mark Carney）甚至被部分批評者稱為「不可靠的男友」，因為他曾暗示利率將會變動，結果卻未發生。儘管面臨這些挑戰，霍爾與伍德福德的研究成果仍是現代經濟政策的主要架構。

paragraphs.en: After receiving the news, Michael Woodford told reporters that he felt 'elated' and called the award a tremendous honor. Jennifer L. Mnookin, the president of Columbia University, praised the researchers for fundamentally reshaping how we understand economic policy. She noted that their work has provided the world with the necessary tools to navigate economic upturns and downturns more effectively.
paragraphs.zh: 得知獲獎消息後，伍德福德告訴記者他感到「欣喜若狂」，並稱此獎項為極大的榮譽。哥倫比亞大學校長努金（Jennifer L. Mnookin）讚揚這兩位研究者從根本上重塑了我們對經濟政策的理解。她指出，他們的研究為世界提供了有效應對經濟起伏所需的必要工具。

paragraphs.en: As the global economy continues to face challenges like energy crises and sudden changes in consumer behavior, the models created by Hall and Woodford remain vital. John Hassler, the chair of the committee for the economics prize, emphasized that the goal for governments is to reduce the size of these economic swings. By understanding the behavior of individuals, policymakers are now better equipped to prevent the economy from getting stuck in a cycle of high unemployment or losing control over inflation. This Nobel Prize recognizes that when people understand what the government is trying to accomplish, the entire economy becomes more stable.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著全球經濟持續面臨能源危機與消費者行為突變等挑戰，霍爾與伍德福德所建立的模型依然至關重要。經濟學獎委員會主席哈斯勒（John Hassler）強調，政府的目標在於縮減這些經濟波動的幅度。透過理解個人的行為，決策者現在更有能力防止經濟陷入高失業率的循環，或失去對通貨膨脹的控制。這項諾貝爾獎肯定了當民眾理解政府的目標時，整體經濟將會變得更加穩定。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To become involved in a difficult situation to help or improve it.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於日常對話，這裡指政府介入經濟調控。文中：After the Great Depression, the economist John Maynard Keynes argued that governments should step in to boost demand when the economy is weak or lower demand when prices rise too quickly.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Methods or tools used to influence or control a system.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （影響或控制系統的）手段、工具。
keyTerms.noteZh: 原意為物理上的「槓桿」，這裡比喻控制經濟的手段。文中：Instead of viewing the economy as a machine that leaders can simply control by pulling levers, their work shows that the economy is shaped by the choices of millions of people who are always looking toward the future.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A communication strategy used by central banks to signal their future monetary policy intentions.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 前瞻指引（央行透過溝通未來利率走向來影響市場預期）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 看似一般的詞組，但在經濟學中是特定術語。文中：This idea led to a tool known as 'forward guidance.'

keyTerms.definitionEn: Unable to move or escape from a particular situation.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 陷入（某種狀態）、動彈不得。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞 stick 的過去分詞，這裡形容經濟陷入惡性循環。文中：By understanding the behavior of individuals, policymakers are now better equipped to prevent the economy from getting stuck in a cycle of high unemployment or losing control over inflation.

quiz.question: According to the article, why did the traditional 'Keynesian recipe' struggle during the 1970s?

options.A: Governments were unable to control interest rates effectively.
options.B: It could not address the simultaneous occurrence of high inflation and high unemployment.
options.C: It failed to account for the impact of the 2008 financial crisis on global markets.
options.D: Businesses were changing their prices too frequently for the model to track.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，凱因斯模型在 1970 年代面臨挑戰，因為當時許多國家同時遭遇高通貨膨脹與高失業率，舊有的模型無法解釋或解決這種現象。選項 A 並非文中提到的主因；選項 C 的 2008 金融危機發生在 1970 年代之後，時間點錯誤；選項 D 則是 Hall 和 Woodford 的研究重點，而非舊模型的缺失。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the role of 'forward guidance' in economic policy?

options.A: It is a guaranteed method to prevent all future economic recessions.
options.B: It requires central banks to hide their future plans to avoid market panic.
options.C: It relies on the assumption that public confidence is influenced by clear communication.
options.D: It was developed primarily to help businesses change their prices more quickly.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第六段提到，透過解釋目標，中央銀行可以讓大眾更有信心，進而維持經濟運作。這暗示了政策制定者的溝通與大眾信心之間存在正相關。選項 A 過於絕對，文中並未保證能預防所有衰退；選項 B 與文章提到「清楚傳達計畫」的目標相反；選項 D 錯誤，因為文中提到企業是因為調整價格成本高才傾向長期規劃，而非為了讓價格調整更快。

quiz.question: In the context of the article, what does the phrase 'dark clouds on the horizon' mean?

options.A: The physical weather conditions affecting agricultural production.
options.B: The literal presence of storm clouds during an economic crisis.
options.C: The anticipation of negative future economic events.
options.D: The confusion caused by unclear government communication.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。在第五段中，作者使用 'dark clouds on the horizon' 作為隱喻，描述家庭對未來收入的擔憂。這是一種慣用語，用來比喻即將到來的潛在危險或負面狀況。選項 A 與 B 皆為字面解釋，不符合經濟學語境；選項 D 雖然提到混亂，但這並非該隱喻所指的「未來擔憂」，而是指政策溝通的結果。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the work of Hall and Woodford?

options.A: They proved that the government should never intervene in the economy.
options.B: They created a new way to stabilize the economy by focusing on individual decision-making and clear communication.
options.C: They are primarily famous for predicting the 2008 financial crisis before it happened.
options.D: They argued that central banks should focus only on controlling interest rates, regardless of public opinion.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。全文旨在介紹 Hall 與 Woodford 的獲獎貢獻，即透過研究個體（家庭與企業）的決策行為，並強調政策制定者透過「前瞻指引」與大眾清楚溝通，來達成經濟穩定。選項 A 與文中提到的政府需管理經濟目標不符；選項 C 文中並未提及他們預測了金融危機；選項 D 忽略了他們強調與公眾溝通的重要性。
